text:
samir: Noticed a surge of ALB 502s hitting the edge pool in us-west-2 starting ~02:15 UTC. Dash shows backend resets and a pile of TIME-WAITs. Possible SNAT exhaustion on NAT GW.
rachael: saw the alert. NAT GW port util jumped to >95% in two AZs. ALB retries amplify the issue. :grimacing:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: us-west-2.edge-pool ALB 5xx rate 11% (5m), NATGW port utilization 96% (5m)
alice: pulling `ss -tin state TIME-WAIT` from edge-41: count ~198k. conntrack shows `used: 245000 entries: 262144`.
mike: can we confirm whether nodes are using per-node SNAT (instance nat) or centralized NAT gateway? last doc says NAT GW.
santiago: confirmed: private nodes -> NAT GW per AZ -> internet. No per-node EIP.
rachael: quick triage: what destinations are creating the egress churn? Model pulls? Telemetry? healthchecks?
alice: pcap and logs show huge bursty connections to telemetry.redwood-telemetry.net and some 3rd-party model registry pulls. Many short-lived POSTs.
samir: can we reduce the fanout temporarily? throttle telemetry batch window? tune backoff on registry pulls?
mike: created a canary patch on one deployment: enable HTTP keepalive on sidecars + connection pooling. Also tuned `tcp_fin_timeout` to 20s and expanded `ip_local_port_range` on 5 nodes.
rachael: those kernel tweaks are helpful but risky at scale. We should do them via playbook and rollback plan.
alice: after the canary, TIME-WAIT on canary nodes dropped from 198k -> 28k in 8 minutes. NAT GW port util in AZ-a for canary subnet dropped ~45%.
santiago: good signal. Rolling keepalive to 30% of fleet and scheduling kernel param rollout to low-risk AZ.
samir: medium-term strategy: 1) add a second NAT GW per AZ to increase simultaneous ports 2) consider placing an egress proxy pool (per-AZ) to multiplex outbound connections 3) mark telemetry endpoints for connection reuse (longer idle keepalives)
mike: also look at ALB healthcheck patterns. If a node briefly fails, ALB retries create retry storms and more outbound egress for health/metrics. We should add jitter and backoff.
rachael: ops task: INFRA-987 created to track NATGW capacity increase + egress-proxy POC + sidecar keepalive rollout. Assigned to eng-infra.
monitoring-bot: NOTE: playbook/egress suggests alert when (conntrack_used > 80% AND timewait_count > 100k AND natgw_port_util > 85%).
alice: provisional mitigation: add one NAT GW in AZ-b and enable route53 latency-based fallback to spread egress across AZs for high-egress subnets.
samir: agree. Also evaluate using NAT instances (with autoscaling) for very high-throughput subnets; gives more ports per instance via additional EIPs.
mike: logging next steps: finish fleet rollout of keepalive, run synthetic SNAT exhaustion test in staging, and wire a composite alert. If we still see >10% 5xxs after 30m, escalate to capacity add.
rachael: current status: canary good, partial rollout 30%, monitoring flagged downward trend. Continue 30m watch, then full roll if stable. :thumbsup:
